newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MANDELA WARNS S.AFRICAN PRESS AGAINST BIAS.
newsitem.headline: MANDELA WARNS S.AFRICAN PRESS AGAINST BIAS.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela renewed his criticism of the South African media on Sunday, saying they appeared to be biased in their reporting of power struggles within his African National Congress.

Feuds have erupted in ANC branches in several provinces in recent months, particularly in Free State where Mandela last month removed the provincial premier who had repeatedly clashed with branch officials.
Asked about suggestions that his intervention had been high- handed, Mandela told a news conference that other political parties expelled members without being criticised in the media.
"If there is any organisation that observes democratic procedures, it is the ANC," he said.
"I just want to warn that we do not want to make accusations against anybody, especially the mass media, that they are prejudiced, that they are biased."
Mandela last month upbraided black journalists who had written critical articles about the ANC, saying they were the puppets of white media bosses who did not like his policies.

"When the ANC observes correct procedures, and takes those procedures in the interest of unity of the organisation which is leading the transformation process, then there is a hue and cry even on the part of the most experienced journalist that there is dictatorship," Mandela said on Sunday.
"It may well that because this is a majority party you pay particular attention. But your comments must be based on scientific investigation."
He was speaking after meeting branch members of the ANC in the Western Cape, one of two provinces -- out of a total of nine -- that the party does not control.
According to a copy of his remarks to the branch officials, he said "the organisational state of affairs in the ANC and its allied formations often leaves much to be desired".
"We all know that a great deal of energy has been consumed on intra-organisational leadership rivalries, personality squabbles and factionalism," he said.
Asked about this at the news conference, Mandela said he was confident the party leadership could address the infighting problems.
"The organisation is united. Unity does not mean we don't have dissidents, the point is those dissidents are not in a position to split the organisation," Mandela said.
